questions.q: What does an Azure Private Endpoint actually create inside your VNet?
options: A network interface with a private IP, mapped to one specific instance of a PaaS resource
A new public IP address dedicated to the resource
A VPN gateway tunnel to the resource's region
A duplicate copy of the PaaS resource inside your subscription
questions.explain: A Private Endpoint is a NIC with a private IP in your own subnet, mapped to one specific resource instance (e.g. one storage account), so traffic never leaves the Microsoft backbone or touches a public IP.

questions.q: What role does a Private DNS Zone play in an Azure Private Endpoint setup?
options: It assigns the Private Endpoint's priority relative to NSG rules
It encrypts traffic between the VNet and the Private Endpoint
It overrides the resource's public FQDN so it resolves to the Private Endpoint's private IP, keeping application connection strings unchanged
It is required only when the Private Endpoint targets Azure SQL, not storage
questions.explain: Without the linked Private DNS Zone, the resource's public FQDN would still resolve publicly; with it, the same FQDN resolves to the Private Endpoint's private IP, so nothing in the application needs to change.

questions.q: On the provider side of AWS PrivateLink, what fronts the service being published as an Endpoint Service?
options: An Application Load Balancer
An API Gateway custom domain
A NAT Gateway
A Network Load Balancer
questions.explain: A PrivateLink Endpoint Service is published by fronting the service with a Network Load Balancer; consumers then reach it through an Interface VPC Endpoint without peering or a public IP.

questions.q: What makes an AWS Gateway Endpoint (used for S3 and DynamoDB) structurally different from an Interface Endpoint?
options: A Gateway Endpoint is a route table entry pointing at the service's prefix list, with no ENI involved, while an Interface Endpoint is an ENI with a private IP
A Gateway Endpoint requires its own Network Load Balancer, just like an Interface Endpoint
A Gateway Endpoint only works across VPC peering connections
A Gateway Endpoint and an Interface Endpoint are functionally identical, just named differently
questions.explain: Gateway Endpoints are route-based, not ENI-based — they add an entry in the route table for the service's IP prefix list, which is why they're free and have no direct Azure equivalent.

questions.q: What is the key security difference between the older Azure Service Endpoint model and a Private Endpoint?
options: Service Endpoints are more expensive to operate than Private Endpoints
Service Endpoints only work with virtual machines, never with PaaS resources
A Service Endpoint still leaves the resource reachable at a public IP (restricted to approved VNets/subnets), while a Private Endpoint removes the public IP from the traffic path entirely
A Private Endpoint cannot be combined with a Private DNS Zone
questions.explain: Service Endpoints restrict which VNet/subnet can reach a resource's public IP over the Microsoft backbone, but the resource still has a public IP in the path; a Private Endpoint removes the public IP entirely.
